(i) sexually dimorphic weaponry can vary seasonally, (ii) the seasonal variation can result from divergent changes between males and females, (iii) this divergence can be due to a trade-off between claw growth and reproductive investment, and (iv) the trade-off can occur in both sexes but in opposite directions.

(1) both male and female weapon size varies seasonally in the snapping shrimp Alpheus angulosuseven though both sexes have a weapon and both sexes compete over the same resources, and (2) the observed seasonal variation in weapon size results from sex differences in the seasonal patterns of investment, with males investing in weapons during the reproductive season and females investing in weapons during a nonreproductive season.
